summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin 38.1.2 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package's package.json declares a preinstall hook ("node setup.mjs") that runs at npm install time. setup.mjs is itself obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (hex identifiers, per-block string alias objects) and downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line heavily obfuscated blob (shuffled numeric string-array constructor with rotator function) that has no relationship to the package's stated purpose of providing custom ESLint rules for React/MobX/TypeScript. The legitimate ESLint rule sources under src/ and dist/ appear intact, indicating a hijack/compromise-style release that grafts a dropper onto an otherwise real library. Fetching an alternate runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled payload at install time evades Node-focused static analysis and is the alternate-runtime-dropper attack shape. Execution is automatic on default `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
